title: Cap. 7 Quartum: sufficienter / efficaciter—death for elect by absolute saving will
pass_a_gloss: A fourth argument will furnish us that most received distinction among all Theologians, by which it is customarily said that Christ died for all sufficiently, for the elect efficaciously. For just as from the former member we refuted the opinion of those who deny that the death of Christ by the decree of God is for all human beings an applicable remedy, so from this latter those are to be refuted who deny that the death of Christ, and that by the decree of God, is a remedy to be applied to the elect efficaciously and infallibly. For what other sense can there be of these words, He died for the elect efficaciously, than, He died with an absolute intention and efficacious will of saving the elect?
pass_b_english: A fourth argument is the distinction most received among all theologians: that Christ died for all sufficiently, for the elect efficaciously. Just as from the first half we refuted those who deny that Christ’s death, by God’s decree, is an applicable remedy for all people, so from the second half those must be refuted who deny that Christ’s death, and that by God’s decree, is a remedy to be applied to the elect efficaciously and infallibly. What else can “He died for the elect efficaciously” mean than that he died with an absolute intention and efficacious will to save the elect?
source_text: Quartum argumentum nobis praebebit receptissima illa inter omnes Theologos distinctio, qua dici solet, Christum pro omnibus mortuum fuisse sufficienter, pro electis mortuum efficaciter. Nam sicuti ex priore membro refutavimus illorum sententiam, qui negant Christi mortem ex decreto Dei esse omnibus hominibus remedium applicabile, ita ex hoc posteriore illi sunt refutandi, qui negant Christi mortem, idque ex decreto Dei, esse remedium electis efficaciter & infallibiliter applicandum. Quis enim potest esse alius sensus horum verborum, Mortuus est pro electis efficaciter, quam, Mortuus est absoluta intentione & efficaci voluntate servandi electos?
